To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thyroid nodules with irregular margins, microcalcifications, hypoechogenicity, hypoechogenecity relative to the strap muscles, and taller-than-wide shape have a high risk of malignancy.
the sonographic features associated with malignancy are microcalcifications, hyperechogenicity, and irregular margins.

the sonographic features that are highly predictive of malignancy in thyroid nodules include the following: hypoechogenicity, irregular or ill-defined margins, microcalcifications, taller-than-wide shape, and absence of a halo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel methods for the analysis of complex data sets.
the study of the structure and function of proteins, and their role in biological systems.
the development of new ultrasound techniques for imaging the thyroid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sonographic characteristics of thyroid nodules are not specific enough to be used as the only criterion to differentiate benign and malignant lesions.
ultrasound is the best imaging technique for evaluating thyroid nodules and is the initial imaging technique of choice for evaluating cervical lymph nodes in patients with thyroid cancer.

thyroid nodules that are hypoechoic, irregular, have a taller-than-wide appearance, have microcalcifications, have a nonhomogenous internal echo pattern, have a spiculated margin, have a rim halo, have an irregular halo, and/or have extracapsular invasion have a greater than 95% likelihood of being malignant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thyroid nodules with suspicious sonographic features are associated with malignancy in 70% of cases and that ultrasound is a useful tool in the management of thyroid cancer patients.
ultrasound is an accurate and cost-effective imaging tool for the evaluation of thyroid nodules.
thyroid ultrasound is an important tool for thyroid nodules characterization, especially for the differentiation of malignant and benign thyroid nodules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sonographic appearance of thyroid nodular disease is not a good predictor of malignancy, and that ultrasound is not a reliable method for distinguishing benign from malignant thyroid nodules.

sonography can be used to differentiate cystic from solid thyroid nodules and that sonography can also be used to characterize the appearance of solid thyroid nodules, with the goal of identifying features that are associated with malignancy.
thyroid nodules that are hyperechoic and have irregular margins, or that are hypovascular on Doppler imaging, are more likely to be malignant.
